subject: English
source: PROVENANCE & VERIFICATION STATUS. (1) Content & Learning Standards: extracted from the official 'DSKP KSSM Bahasa Inggeris Tingkatan 1 (CEFR v2)' hosted on AnyFlip (https://anyflip.com/iaciy/mjkn/ pages 26-76) and cross-checked against studylib (https://studylib.net/doc/26070759/) and Studocu (https://www.studocu.com/my/document/.../dskp-form-1-skills-simplified/78585457). VERIFICATION STATUS: MOSTLY VERIFIED against the official DSKP PDF wording. Some sub-standards that are blank/dashed in the Form 1 table (e.g. 1.1.3, 1.3.1, 2.2.1/2.2.2, 3.1.5) were reported by the source as having no Learning Standard at Form 1 level and are therefore omitted here; a teacher should confirm against the printed DSKP before relying on completeness. (2) CEFR target A2 Mid (Revised) per the DSKP KSSM Form 1 CEFR v2 document (BPK/KPM) as reported by the AnyFlip/SlideShare copies. (3) Textbook & units: 'Pulse 2' (Macmillan), the official KSSM Form 1 & 2 coursebook; Form 1 covers the Starter unit plus Units 1-5 (titles from anyflip.com/kdisn/stws, sites.google.com/moe-dl.edu.my/pulse2, and Wordwall/Quizlet unit resources). VERIFIED. (4) theme_topics mapping: RECONSTRUCTED by aligning the 4 DSKP themes to the Pulse 2 units - needs teacher verification. (5) rpt: RECONSTRUCTED from the Form 1 English KSSM Scheme of Work (11-lesson-per-unit cycle, ~112 sixty-minute lessons; mhdazlan.wordpress.com/.../04-secondary-scheme-of-work-form-1.pdf and slideshare.net/.../english-schemes-of-work-for-form-1-kssm-2024). It is NOT a verbatim official RPT/RPH - it is a sensible week-by-week mapping of the Pulse 2 units across a ~40-week school year and MUST be adjusted to the school calendar and verified by the teacher.
_note_theme_topics: Maps each DSKP theme to the Pulse 2 (Form 1) units most relevant to it. A unit may appear under more than one theme because units often cover several themes. Form 1 Pulse 2 units concentrate on People/Culture, Health/Environment and Science/Technology; Consumerism & Financial Awareness is only lightly touched at Form 1 and is developed more in Form 2. Teachers can edit this mapping freely.
language_focus_examples: Countable and uncountable nouns; quantifiers (some, any, much, many)
will / be going to for future plans and predictions
Modal verbs (can, must, should) for rules, obligation and advice
there is / there are; prepositions of place and time
_note_structure: Keys 'bidang' (=Skill), 'standard_kandungan' (=Content Standard) and 'standard_pembelajaran' (=Learning Standard) reuse the engine's keys. Wording matches the official DSKP KSSM Form 1 (CEFR v2). Where a Content Standard has no Learning Standard at Form 1 level in the official table, it is omitted.

standard_kandungan.nama: Understand meaning in a variety of familiar contexts

standard_pembelajaran.huraian: Understand with little or no support the main ideas in simple longer texts on a range of familiar topics.
Understand with little or no support specific information and details in simple longer texts on a range of familiar topics.
Understand longer sequences of supported classroom instructions.
Understand more complex supported questions.
Understand with support longer simple narratives on a wide range of familiar topics.

standard_kandungan.nama: Use appropriate listening strategies in a variety of contexts

standard_pembelajaran.huraian: Guess the meaning of unfamiliar words from clues provided by other known words and by context.

standard_kandungan.nama: Communicate information, ideas, opinions and feelings intelligibly on familiar topics

standard_pembelajaran.huraian: Ask about and give detailed information about themselves and others.
Ask about and express rules and obligations.
Ask about and describe future plans or events.
Explain and give reasons for simple advice.
Ask about and describe personality.
Keep interaction going in short exchanges by checking understanding of what a speaker is saying.
Agree on a set of basic steps needed to complete extended classroom tasks.

standard_kandungan.nama: Communicate appropriately to a small or large group on familiar topics

standard_pembelajaran.huraian: Narrate short stories, events and experiences.

standard_kandungan.nama: Understand a variety of texts by using a range of appropriate reading strategies to construct meaning

standard_pembelajaran.huraian: Understand the main points in simple longer texts.
Understand specific details and information in simple longer texts.
Guess the meaning of unfamiliar words from clues provided by other known words and by context.
Use with some support familiar print and digital resources to check meaning.

standard_kandungan.nama: Explore and expand ideas for personal development by reading independently and widely

standard_pembelajaran.huraian: Read and enjoy fiction / non-fiction and other suitable print and digital texts of interest.

standard_kandungan.nama: Communicate intelligibly through print and digital media on familiar topics

standard_pembelajaran.huraian: Give detailed information about themselves and others.
Describe future plans or events.
Narrate factual and imagined events and experiences.
Describe personality.
Connect sentences into two coherent paragraphs or more using basic coordinating conjunctions and reference pronouns.

standard_kandungan.nama: Communicate with appropriate language, form and style

standard_pembelajaran.huraian: Use capitals, full stops, commas in lists, question marks, and speech marks appropriately at discourse level.
Spell most high frequency words accurately in independent writing.
Produce a plan or draft of two paragraphs or more and modify this appropriately in response to feedback.

standard_kandungan.nama: Engage with, respond to and interpret a variety of literary text types

standard_pembelajaran.huraian: Describe in simple language a character's actions or feelings and explain the reasons for them.
Identify and describe in simple language the key characters in a text.

standard_kandungan.nama: Express an imaginative response to literary texts

standard_pembelajaran.huraian: Respond imaginatively and intelligibly through creating simple stories.

_note_rpt: RECONSTRUCTED week-by-week plan (~40 weeks) built by distributing the Pulse 2 Form 1 units (Starter + Units 1-5, ~11 lessons per unit / 112 sixty-minute lessons total) across a typical Malaysian school year, with allowance for orientation, mid/end-of-term assessments and holidays. This is NOT a verbatim official RPT - align to the school's academic calendar (takwim) and verify before use. standard_kandungan lists the Content Standard codes emphasised that week.

rpt.catatan: Orientation; diagnostic; revision of greetings, personal information, be/have got, classroom language.
Revise present simple, question words; write a short self-introduction.
Likes/dislikes, free-time activities; present simple and adverbs of frequency.
Present continuous vs present simple; talking about hobbies and preferences.
Write about yourself and your interests; describing personality.
Respond to a short literary text; class survey/presentation on likes.
Stories, media and reality vs fiction; past simple (regular verbs).
Past simple irregular verbs; narrating events.
Narrate a factual or imagined event; sequencing a short story.
First-term revision and formative assessment (Units 1-2).
Explore characters in a short story; create a simple story.
Weather and natural events; comparative adjectives.
Superlative adjectives; describing extreme weather.
Write a short report/description of weather in different places.
Group task: weather forecast role-play/presentation.
Respond to a poem/story linked to nature and weather.
Mid-year revision (Units 1-3).
Mid-year examination week.
Mid-year school holiday (adjust to takwim).
Animals, habitats and the natural world; countable/uncountable nouns.
Quantifiers (some, any, much, many); describing quantities.
Write a factual paragraph about an animal or habitat.
Group project: endangered species / environment awareness.
Engage with a literary text on nature; imaginative response.
Formative assessment (Unit 4).
Science, experiments and inventions; will / be going to for predictions.
Future forms; giving instructions for a simple process.
Write the steps of a simple experiment or process.
Plan and present a simple experiment/demonstration in groups.
Respond to a science-themed literary text; create a simple story.
Extension: spending money on hobbies/experiments; needs vs wants (lightly touched at Form 1).
Consolidation and reteaching of weaker standards across units.
End-of-year revision (Units 1-5).
Exam skills practice; reading and writing focus.
End-of-year examination week.
Post-exam discussion; feedback; drama/story project.
Language games, presentations, class literature performance.
Mini-project / e-portfolio; 21st century skills task.
Self-reflection on the year; compile portfolio; peer feedback.
Year-end school holiday (adjust to takwim).
